newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BAF BACKS WEMBLEY AS SITE FOR NEW STADIUM.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAF BACKS WEMBLEY AS SITE FOR NEW STADIUM.

text.p: The British Athletic Federation (BAF) said on Monday it wanted to see Britain's proposed new national stadium built at Wembley rather than Manchester.

"It is our ambition to stage major world and European events and our international colleagues tell us London -- and in particular Wembley with its rich sporting history -- would have an outstanding chance in any bidding process," BAF executive chairman Peter Radford said.

He said a revamped all-purpose stadium at Wembley, the venue for England soccer internationals, would enhance the BAF's planned bid for the 2001 world athletics championships as well as any future Olympic bid by London.
"It would be appropriate for the major Olympic sport to rekindle interest in an Olympic Games in London in the opening decade of the next millennium," said Radford.
A final decision on the site of the proposed stadium is expected before the end of the year, with London and Manchester as the only two options.
Manchester, which saw its bids for the 1996 and 2000 Olympic Games fail, says Britain's sporting facilities should be redistributed away from the capital.
London claims it is the only city in Britain capable of staging an event as big as the Olympics.
